title: What the guarded media fetch refuses, and under which code
pins: Which URLs `fetchPublicUrlContent()` refuses, and under WHICH CODE, in every language. The code is the contract â€” a consumer switches on it to decide whether to widen an allow-list, surface a hard stop, or report an SSRF attempt. The message is deliberately not pinned: the three implementations word these differently on purpose, and a test over the prose holds every language to a translation and reddens on a wording improvement that changed nothing. Same decision as `browser-url-policy`, and the same spellings â€” `private_address_refused` is one finding with one name across the ecosystem.
scope: The refusal decision and stable code of the opt-in guarded media fetch. PHP and TypeScript retain their pre-existing unguarded fetch methods, exercised by url-0009; Python has no unguarded fetch method by design. This suite does not establish byte handling or complete SSRF protection: a name can resolve differently between the check and the request, which only connection-level pinning closes.
findings: Writing this corpus exposed the need for machine-readable refusal codes; the PHP reference gained them in prism 07f842b. The TypeScript and Python guards now reproduce the ten recorded refusal outcomes and the successful public-fetch control. This establishes agreement for those inputs, with initial refusals sending no request and the refused redirect target never requested; it does not establish that every URL is safe or that an identical defect cannot exist in all three implementations. PHP and TypeScript alone exercise url-0009: Python explicitly skips the legacy unguarded-path control because that API never existed there, so agrees remains false on that row. DNS rebinding between validation and connection remains unclosed in all three guards. All five refusal codes are now compared in the common corpus. url-0012 repeats a public self-redirect in every fake response and records too_many_redirects from all three runners; its six-request assertion pins the default allowance at five redirect hops in every language. Each behavioral suite also retains a successful chain within the bound as a discrimination control (G-71).

discrimination.note: url-0001 fetches successfully and distinguishes a guard that refuses everything. url-0009 preserves the existing unguarded loopback path in PHP and TypeScript; Python has no such path.

py.note: url-0009 is explicitly skipped for py: no unguarded media fetch exists by design.
